content: The APPL2 gene encodes a protein in humans known as DCC-interacting protein 13-beta. To study the function of the APPL2 gene, model organisms have been utilized. Specifically, a conditional knockout mouse line, designated as Appl2tm1a(KOMP)Wtsi, was developed. This was part of the International Knockout Mouse Consortium program, a large-scale mutagenesis initiative aimed at creating and distributing animal models of human diseases for research purposes. The mouse line was generated at the Wellcome Trust Sanger Institute. Both male and female mice from this knockout line underwent a standardized series of phenotypic assessments to evaluate the consequences of the gene deletion. A total of 23 distinct tests were conducted on these mutant mice. However, no significant abnormalities were identified in the results of these tests.
